stages.title: Read and define the problem
stages.description: Turn a story into a precise, testable task.

stages.title: Represent the problem
stages.description: Choose a clear model for the information and relationships.

stages.title: Build reliable logic
stages.description: Construct decisions, rules and deterministic solution steps.

stages.title: Work with sequences and patterns
stages.description: Reason about repeated actions, ranges and common sequence patterns.

stages.title: Choose data structures
stages.description: Select representations based on the operations a problem needs.

stages.title: Search, order and select
stages.description: Recognise when searching, sorting, filtering and merging fit.

stages.title: Solve recursive and graph problems
stages.description: Handle hierarchical, connected and dependency-based problems.

stages.title: Reason about efficiency
stages.description: Compare cost, scale, memory and practical trade-offs.

stages.title: Prove, test and review
stages.description: Check correctness, diagnose defects and evaluate AI-assisted output.

stages.title: Transfer to real-world interviews
stages.description: Apply the full problem-solving process to unfamiliar scenarios.

modules.title: Separate the story from the task
modules.objective: Identify the exact outcome requested without confusing background details with the task or its possible implementation.
modules.focus: Story versus task; input; action; output
modules.evidence: A one-sentence task statement that preserves the requested outcome.

modules.title: Express a task as input, rule and output
modules.objective: Describe a problem as the information received, the transformation required and the result expected.
modules.evidence: A complete input–rule–output contract.

modules.title: Extract constraints and limits
modules.objective: Find size, range, uniqueness, ordering and resource restrictions that change which solutions are valid.
modules.evidence: A constraint sheet that distinguishes explicit limits from assumptions.

modules.title: Separate facts, assumptions and unknowns
modules.objective: Distinguish what the problem guarantees from what a solver is tempted to assume, and identify what must be clarified.
modules.evidence: A list of confirmed facts, open questions and safe assumptions.

modules.title: Use examples and counterexamples
modules.objective: Create examples that confirm the interpretation and counterexamples that expose an incomplete or incorrect reading.
modules.evidence: A small example set with independently reasoned expected results.

modules.title: Discover edge cases before solving
modules.objective: Identify empty, minimal, maximal, repeated, missing and unusual inputs relevant to a task.
modules.focus: Boundary cases; duplicates; missing values; extremes
modules.evidence: A ranked edge-case list with a reason each case matters.

modules.title: Write observable acceptance criteria
modules.objective: Convert a vague request into conditions that a proposed result must satisfy to be considered correct.
modules.evidence: Testable acceptance criteria that can be checked without seeing the implementation.

modules.title: Decompose a task into subproblems
modules.objective: Break a multi-part request into smaller outcomes that can be solved and checked independently.
modules.evidence: A dependency-aware breakdown of a larger task.

modules.title: Map dependencies between subproblems
modules.objective: Determine which outputs are needed before other steps can begin and identify independent work.
modules.evidence: A valid execution order with dependencies explained.

modules.title: Turn an unclear request into a precise brief
modules.objective: Resolve a realistic, imperfect problem statement into a bounded task with inputs, outputs, constraints and acceptance criteria.
modules.evidence: A complete problem brief and a justified list of unresolved questions.

modules.title: Identify entities and their attributes
modules.objective: Extract the objects a problem talks about and the information that describes each one.
modules.evidence: An entity model that distinguishes identity from descriptive fields.

modules.title: Distinguish single values from collections
modules.objective: Recognise whether a task needs one value, an ordered collection, a group of unique values or keyed records.
modules.evidence: A suitable first-pass data representation for several scenarios.

modules.title: Choose between a sequence and a set
modules.objective: Decide whether order and duplicates are meaningful or whether only membership and uniqueness matter.
modules.evidence: A representation choice justified by required operations.

modules.title: Model direct lookup with key–value records
modules.objective: Represent information that must be found quickly by a stable identifier or key.
modules.evidence: A key–value model with a clear uniqueness rule.

modules.title: Model last-in and first-in workflows
modules.objective: Recognise when a stack-like or queue-like process matches the order in which work must be handled.
modules.evidence: A correct workflow model and a trace of its state changes.

modules.title: Represent state and state transitions
modules.objective: Describe how an object or process changes after an event, while identifying valid and invalid states.
modules.evidence: A state-transition model with allowed transitions identified.

modules.title: Represent relationships as a network
modules.objective: Model entities connected by relationships when a problem concerns reachability, routes or dependencies.
modules.evidence: A relationship model with correctly identified nodes and edges.

modules.title: Trace information with tables and diagrams
modules.objective: Use a state table, decision table or simple diagram to make a multi-step process visible and checkable.
modules.focus: Trace tables; decision tables; state diagrams
modules.evidence: A complete trace that another person can follow.

modules.title: Choose a representation from required operations
modules.objective: Select a data model by asking what must be looked up, updated, ordered, counted or traversed.
modules.evidence: A reasoned model choice based on the dominant operations.

modules.title: Model a practical domain
modules.objective: Translate a small business workflow into entities, relationships, state and operations without relying on a programming language.
modules.evidence: A coherent model of a realistic workflow.

modules.title: Write steps in an unambiguous order
modules.objective: Describe a deterministic procedure where each step has a clear purpose and no hidden interpretation.
modules.evidence: An ordered procedure that produces the intended result on a sample.

modules.title: Use conditions to make decisions
modules.objective: Translate a requirement into a condition and determine which outcome follows when it is true or false.
modules.evidence: A correct decision rule for each case.

modules.title: Combine conditions without logic errors
modules.objective: Evaluate compound conditions and identify how AND, OR and NOT affect the result.
modules.focus: Compound logic; truth tables; short-circuit intuition
modules.evidence: A complete truth table and correct interpretation of a compound rule.

modules.title: Count, accumulate and maintain a running result
modules.objective: Distinguish a counter from a running total and update each correctly as records are processed.
modules.evidence: A correct state trace for a count or aggregate.

modules.title: Compare values and maintain a best-so-far result
modules.objective: Design reasoning for minimum, maximum and selection tasks, including ties and empty input conditions.
modules.evidence: A correct comparison strategy with boundary behaviour stated.

modules.title: Build multi-branch classification rules
modules.objective: Translate several categories and thresholds into mutually clear decision rules, including boundary values.
modules.focus: Decision trees; ranges; precedence; boundary ownership
modules.evidence: A complete decision table with no gaps or overlapping rules.

modules.title: Use preconditions, postconditions and invariants
modules.objective: State what must be true before a procedure, what it guarantees after, and what remains true during it.
modules.evidence: A concise correctness contract for a procedure.

modules.title: Respect operation order and side effects
modules.objective: Recognise when changing the order of steps changes the outcome and identify operations that mutate shared state.
modules.evidence: A safe operation order with side effects called out.

modules.title: Distinguish local choices from global goals
modules.objective: Recognise when a locally attractive decision can block a better overall outcome and when a greedy choice is justified.
modules.focus: Greedy choice; look-ahead; local versus global
modules.evidence: A reasoned decision about whether a local-choice strategy is safe.

modules.title: Construct a complete decision workflow
modules.objective: Combine conditions, counters, comparisons and invariants to solve a deterministic multi-step task.
modules.evidence: A traceable procedure with correct results across varied cases.

modules.title: Trace repeated actions as changing state
modules.objective: Track how each repetition changes values and identify the exact state after a specified number of steps.
modules.evidence: A correct step-by-step trace without executing code.

modules.title: Determine when repetition should stop
modules.objective: Define a termination condition and recognise procedures that stop too early, too late or never.
modules.evidence: A valid stop condition and an explanation of why progress reaches it.

modules.title: Prevent off-by-one boundary errors
modules.objective: Reason precisely about inclusive and exclusive endpoints, first and last positions and counts of items.
modules.evidence: Correct start, stop and count decisions on boundary examples.

modules.title: Reason about nested repetition
modules.objective: Count how many operations occur when one repeated process is placed inside another.
modules.focus: Nested repetition; iteration counts; growth intuition
modules.evidence: A correct operation count for nested patterns.

modules.title: Scan from both ends with two pointers
modules.objective: Recognise problems where two moving positions can replace repeated rescanning.
modules.focus: Two pointers; opposing and same-direction scans
modules.evidence: A pointer-movement plan with a clear stopping condition.

modules.title: Process contiguous ranges with a sliding window
modules.objective: Maintain a summary over a moving contiguous range without rebuilding it from scratch each time.
modules.focus: Sliding window; fixed and variable windows
modules.evidence: A window-update trace and a justified validity condition.

modules.title: Use prefix summaries for repeated range questions
modules.objective: Precompute cumulative information so multiple range queries can be answered efficiently.
modules.focus: Prefix sums; cumulative summaries; range queries
modules.evidence: A correct prefix model and range-result derivation.

modules.title: Count frequencies and handle duplicates
modules.objective: Use frequency information to solve counting, matching and repeated-item problems.
modules.evidence: A frequency model with correct counts for repeated values.

modules.title: Reason about intervals and overlapping time windows
modules.objective: Compare, sort and combine ranges when appointments, events or time periods overlap.
modules.evidence: A correct interval classification or merge plan.

modules.title: Select a sequence pattern for an unfamiliar task
modules.objective: Choose between a direct scan, two pointers, a window, prefix summary or frequency model based on the task structure.
modules.evidence: A pattern choice supported by the input structure and required output.

modules.title: Use lists and arrays for ordered data
modules.objective: Reason about position, traversal, insertion, deletion and repeated access in an ordered collection.
modules.evidence: A correct operation plan for an ordered collection.

modules.title: Use maps for direct lookup
modules.objective: Choose a key-based mapping when a problem repeatedly asks for information by identifier.
modules.evidence: A map-based solution outline and its lookup/update behaviour.

modules.title: Use sets for uniqueness and membership
modules.objective: Remove duplicate representation from the reasoning and answer membership questions without preserving order.
modules.evidence: A correct set operation plan with order limitations stated.

modules.title: Use a stack for unresolved work
modules.objective: Model nested or most-recent-first tasks using a last-in-first-out structure.
modules.evidence: A stack trace that preserves the correct processing order.

modules.title: Use a queue for arrival-order processing
modules.objective: Model first-in-first-out work such as service desks, task buffers and breadth-first exploration.
modules.evidence: A queue model and a correct sequence of processed items.

modules.title: Understand linked records and references
modules.objective: Reason about nodes connected by references and the consequences of inserting, removing or losing a link.
modules.evidence: A correct linked-structure update sequence.

modules.title: Prioritise work with a priority queue
modules.objective: Choose a priority-based structure when the next item is selected by urgency or rank rather than arrival time.
modules.focus: Priority; heap intuition; repeated best-item retrieval
modules.evidence: A priority-processing plan with tie and update behaviour considered.

modules.title: Represent hierarchy with trees
modules.objective: Model parent-child relationships and reason about root, leaves, depth and traversal requirements.
modules.evidence: A tree model and a valid traversal plan.

modules.title: Combine structures to support different operations
modules.objective: Use one structure for ordered output and another for fast lookup or counting when a task needs both.
modules.evidence: A composite model that supports all required operations.

modules.title: Choose a data structure from an operation profile
modules.objective: Compare realistic operation frequency, ordering needs and update patterns before selecting a representation.
modules.evidence: A defensible structure choice for an unfamiliar scenario.

modules.title: Search an unsorted collection
modules.objective: Use a systematic scan, decide when it can stop and identify what result must be retained.
modules.focus: Linear search; early exit; matching condition
modules.evidence: A correct search trace and stopping rule.

modules.title: Use binary search only when its preconditions hold
modules.objective: Recognise the sorted or monotonic condition required for repeatedly narrowing a search range.
modules.evidence: A valid range-narrowing trace with its precondition stated.

modules.title: Use sorting to expose structure
modules.objective: Choose sorting when ordered neighbours, ranked output or a later scan makes the task simpler.
modules.evidence: A reasoned decision to sort or avoid sorting.

modules.title: Handle stable order and tie-breaking
modules.objective: Understand when equal-key records must retain their original order or follow a secondary rule.
modules.evidence: A correct sort-order specification including ties.

modules.title: Find the top items without repeatedly sorting everything
modules.objective: Choose an appropriate strategy for selecting a small number of highest-ranked items from a larger collection.
modules.evidence: A selection strategy justified by k and input size.

modules.title: Filter, partition and group records
modules.objective: Separate records by predicates and organise them by categories without losing the intended relationship to each record.
modules.evidence: A correct grouping plan with all records accounted for.

modules.title: Merge two already ordered streams
modules.objective: Combine two sorted sequences into one sorted result while preserving all required items.
modules.evidence: A complete merge trace with correct ordering and multiplicity.

modules.title: Merge overlapping intervals
modules.objective: Sort and combine overlapping ranges while retaining non-overlapping ranges correctly.
modules.evidence: A valid interval merge result for touching and overlapping cases.

modules.title: Combine search with frequency information
modules.objective: Use counts or indexes to answer lookup and multiplicity questions without repeatedly scanning all records.
modules.evidence: A combined representation and lookup strategy.

modules.title: Choose between search and selection strategies
modules.objective: Compare scans, sorting, binary search, hashing and partial selection under their actual preconditions.
modules.evidence: A strategy matrix tied to input properties and required operations.

modules.title: Understand recursion as a smaller version of the same task
modules.objective: Identify a smaller subproblem, the progress toward it and the condition that ends the recursive process.
modules.evidence: A recursive problem definition with a terminating base case.

modules.title: Build a divide-and-conquer solution
modules.objective: Split a problem into smaller parts, solve them and combine their results.
modules.evidence: A decomposition and merge plan with all subproblems covered.

modules.title: Explore alternatives with backtracking
modules.objective: Model decisions as choices, explore a path and undo a choice when it cannot lead to a valid solution.
modules.evidence: A search tree with valid pruning and backtracking steps.

modules.title: Traverse a tree depth first
modules.objective: Choose preorder, inorder, postorder or a general depth-first visit order to answer a tree question.
modules.evidence: A correct traversal sequence and explanation of the chosen order.

modules.title: Explore a tree or graph level by level
modules.objective: Use breadth-first reasoning when distance in edges or nearest-level discovery matters.
modules.evidence: A breadth-first traversal with correct visitation order.

modules.title: Model a graph from a real relationship problem
modules.objective: Translate locations, users, dependencies or connections into vertices and edges with direction and weight where needed.
modules.evidence: A graph model that preserves the domain relationships.

modules.title: Detect reachability and cycles
modules.objective: Determine whether one entity can reach another and whether a path returns to a previously visited state.
modules.evidence: A correct reachability/cycle reasoning trace.

modules.title: Order tasks with dependencies
modules.objective: Identify a valid order for tasks that must follow prerequisite tasks and detect impossible dependency cycles.
modules.evidence: A valid dependency order or a justified cycle diagnosis.

modules.title: Reason about shortest paths
modules.objective: Distinguish unweighted shortest path from weighted shortest path and identify when a simple level search is insufficient.
modules.focus: Shortest path; distance; weights; nonnegative costs
modules.evidence: A suitable shortest-path method choice with assumptions stated.

modules.title: Solve a graph-based scenario
modules.objective: Select a graph representation and traversal strategy for a practical connectivity, dependency or routing problem.
modules.evidence: A complete graph problem plan with a testable result.

modules.title: Count operations instead of timing a machine
modules.objective: Estimate how the number of elementary operations changes with input size.
modules.evidence: A correct operation-count model for a simple procedure.

modules.title: Interpret common growth rates
modules.objective: Compare constant, logarithmic, linear, linearithmic, quadratic and exponential growth conceptually.
modules.evidence: A correct growth-rate ranking and explanation.

modules.title: Compare time and memory trade-offs
modules.objective: Evaluate whether extra storage can reduce repeated work or whether memory constraints favour recomputation.
modules.evidence: A trade-off recommendation grounded in constraints.

modules.title: Estimate nested and sequential costs
modules.objective: Combine operation counts for sequential steps and nested repetition without relying on code syntax.
modules.evidence: A correct overall complexity estimate.

modules.title: Compare scanning, sorting and hashing costs
modules.objective: Choose a strategy based on the number of queries, update frequency, input properties and memory budget.
modules.evidence: A method comparison with preconditions and costs stated.

modules.title: Select structures for scale
modules.objective: Re-evaluate a data structure choice when the input grows or the operation mix changes.
modules.evidence: A structure choice that remains plausible at the stated scale.

modules.title: Establish a brute-force baseline before optimising
modules.objective: Create a simple correct baseline and identify the repeated work an optimisation should remove.
modules.evidence: A correct baseline and a specific, justified improvement.

modules.title: Solve under streaming and memory constraints
modules.objective: Reason about data that arrives incrementally and cannot all be retained in memory.
modules.evidence: A one-pass or bounded-memory strategy with stated limitations.

modules.title: Evaluate caching and recomputation
modules.objective: Decide when stored results are worth their memory, invalidation and staleness risks.
modules.evidence: A caching decision with correctness and freshness conditions.

modules.title: Optimise a solution without breaking its contract
modules.objective: Improve an approach under explicit time and memory constraints while preserving required behaviour.
modules.evidence: A before/after plan with preserved acceptance criteria.

modules.title: Turn requirements into test cases
modules.objective: Derive tests from normal behaviour, boundaries, constraints and acceptance criteria.
modules.evidence: A small, high-value test set linked to requirements.

modules.title: Design boundary and adversarial tests
modules.objective: Construct cases that challenge assumptions, expose overflow, duplicates, ordering errors and worst-case patterns.
modules.evidence: An adversarial test set with the defect each case targets.

modules.title: Use invariants to argue correctness
modules.objective: Explain why a procedure remains correct at each step by identifying a property that must always hold.
modules.evidence: A coherent correctness argument for a short procedure.

modules.title: Trace a defect to its source
modules.objective: Use observed output, intermediate states and a minimal failing case to narrow a defect to its source.
modules.evidence: A defect hypothesis supported by a reproducible trace.

modules.title: Diagnose a wrong algorithm, not just a wrong line
modules.objective: Recognise when a solution strategy fails for a class of inputs even if individual statements appear reasonable.
modules.evidence: A counterexample and a corrected high-level approach.

modules.title: Check regressions and unintended side effects
modules.objective: Verify that a proposed change fixes the target issue without breaking earlier behaviour or altering unrelated data.
modules.focus: Regression; side effects; scope of change
modules.evidence: A regression checklist with targeted tests.

modules.title: Handle missing, malformed and inconsistent data
modules.objective: Choose safe behaviour for absent fields, invalid formats, duplicate identifiers and contradictory records.
modules.evidence: A defensive data-handling policy with explicit outcomes.

modules.title: Review generated code or pseudocode critically
modules.objective: Inspect a supplied solution for requirement mismatch, faulty assumptions, hidden complexity and missing tests.
modules.focus: Code review; requirement fit; correctness; complexity
modules.evidence: A review containing specific defects, evidence and recommended changes.

modules.title: Verify an AI suggestion independently
modules.objective: Treat AI output as a proposal, then validate its assumptions, behaviour, edge cases and evidence before accepting it.
modules.focus: AI output evaluation; independent testing; steering
modules.evidence: A keep/change/reject decision backed by tests and reasoning.

modules.title: Make an engineering judgement under uncertainty
modules.objective: Balance correctness, risk, scope, maintainability and time when information is incomplete.
modules.evidence: A recommendation with assumptions, trade-offs and a validation plan.

modules.title: Solve an event-registration data problem
modules.objective: Count distinct participants from noisy form submissions while preserving the source data and stating the output contract.
modules.evidence: A complete approach and tests for repeated, empty and unique records.

modules.title: Resolve booking and schedule conflicts
modules.objective: Detect overlapping reservations and propose a correct conflict policy for time-based records.
modules.evidence: A schedule-conflict approach with endpoint rules and tests.

modules.title: Reason about inventory changes and audit trails
modules.objective: Track stock movements without losing the distinction between current quantity and historical events.
modules.evidence: A stock-update model and an auditable validation approach.

modules.title: Plan deliveries with routes and capacity constraints
modules.objective: Model delivery stops and constraints, then reason about feasible routes and priorities.
modules.evidence: A route-planning strategy with assumptions and feasibility checks.

modules.title: Design a search and ranking workflow
modules.objective: Separate filtering eligibility from ranking relevance and define how ties and missing attributes are handled.
modules.evidence: A defensible search-and-ranking pipeline.

modules.title: Investigate logs, alerts and an incident
modules.objective: Use event sequences and symptoms to isolate a likely failure point and prioritise checks.
modules.focus: Event ordering; aggregation; root cause; triage
modules.evidence: An incident investigation plan with evidence and next tests.

modules.title: Interpret an unfamiliar task and code excerpt
modules.objective: Read an unfamiliar code or pseudocode fragment, infer its behaviour and relate it to a practical requirement.
modules.evidence: A behaviour trace, requirement check and defect hypothesis.

modules.title: Plan, build and review under changing requirements
modules.objective: Organise a solution when requirements evolve, distinguish essential changes from scope creep and revise tests.
modules.evidence: A revised plan with changed assumptions, tests and review notes.

modules.title: Timed mixed problem-solving assessment
modules.objective: Solve unfamiliar tasks under interview-style time pressure using comprehension, modelling, algorithm choice and verification.
modules.evidence: A timed solution dossier and a gap analysis across competencies.

modules.title: End-to-end problem-solving capstone
modules.objective: Independently interpret, model, choose, express, test, verify and defend a solution to a novel scenario without writing code.
modules.evidence: A complete, evidence-backed solution dossier scored against a common rubric.
